    • Mortgage rates are back up this week, wiping out modest relief from a monthlong drop that began in mid-October.
    • Recent findings suggest that the average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage shot up 29 basis points to 7.28% APR in the week ending Nov.
    • A mortgage is a significant ol’ loan, so when rates go up, those fractions of a percentage point add up fast.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mortgage rates are back up this week, wiping out modest relief from a monthlong drop that began in mid-October.

    Recent findings suggest that the average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage shot up 29 basis points to 7.28% APR in the week ending Nov. 19, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.) We calculate our weekly average using daily APRs recorded over the past five business days.

    A mortgage is a significant ol’ loan, so when rates go up, those fractions of a percentage point add up fast. Say you’re borrowing $400,000 on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage. Compared with last week, your monthly principal and interest payment would be about $78 higher today.

    One bad week doesn't make a trend, but a jump like this can make putting your house hunt on hold until spring feel like a safer bet. So … is it?

    Before deciding whether to buy a house now or wait, it helps to know what's pushing mortgage rates higher.

    In a recent development, right now, mortgage rates are still feeling the aftershocks from two major inflation reports last week. First, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) demonstrated consumer prices rose more than expected in October. Then, the Producer Price Index (PPI) showed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its biggest annual increase in nearly four years.

    Industry observers note that while CPI shows how prices have changed, PPI can offer clues about what's coming next. Faced with higher costs, businesses may raise their own prices to compensate, keeping inflation elevated. Federal Reserve policymakers aren't expecting much relief anytime soon, either. According to meeting minutes released Nov. 18, they expect inflation to remain elevated above their 2% target for a while.

    It has been revealed that to cool rising prices, the Fed can raise the federal funds rate, which is the benchmark interest rate banks charge each other for overnight loans. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. A rate hike is widely expected at the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting.

    According to recent reports, even after a Fed rate hike, there’s no telling how quickly inflation will cool — or whether mortgage rates will follow. (Inflation is just one of many forces that affect mortgage rates, after all.) So if you do wait until spring to buy a house, don't do it just because you're betting on a cheaper mortgage.

    Industry observers note that if you're not in a rush to move, winter can be a good time to regroup. Fewer homes typically go up for sale from November through February, so waiting until spring could give you more options.

    According to recent reports, but latest data from the National Association of Realtors suggests this year's slowdown goes beyond the usual seasonal lull. High mortgage rates and home prices are making it tough for many buyers to make the numbers work. For some buyers, waiting isn't a strategy — it's the only option.

    Pending home sales, a measure of homes under contract, fell 16.7% in October compared with a year earlier, NAR reports. All four U.S. regions saw declines. At this rate, NAR chief economist Lawrence Yun warned that annual home sales could fall to their lowest level since the mid-1990s.

    “Either sizable housing demand is building in the background, or the dream of homeownership is increasingly out of reach for many Americans,” Yun stated in a news release.

    It has been revealed that whether you're waiting by choice or necessity, you can use the time to strengthen your finances. Paying down debt, strengthening your credit score or saving for a bigger down payment could help you qualify for a better mortgage deal.

    Every little bit helps when today’s mortgage rates are this high.

    Mortgage preapprovals typically expire after 60 to 90 days. If you're already preapproved, why not keep an eye on listings this winter? (Hey, I’m an optimist. All it takes is one house.).

    It has been revealed that think like a seller for a second. If you're listing your house in the dead of winter, you're probably not doing it just for fun. You might have a deadline, and you’re probably more willing to negotiate. In the winter, buyers have less competition — and more room to negotiate a lower price, closing cost credits or repairs. Those savings on the sticker price might help offset today's higher borrowing costs.

    Spring typically brings more homes for sale, but it also brings more buyers competing for them. And if mortgage rates end up dropping this spring, you won't be the only one coming out of hibernation.

    10 stocks we like better than Colgate-Palmolive ›.

    Choosing between a steady staples giant and a premium apparel leader requires balancing reliability against growth potential. Investors must decide if Colgate-Palmolive (CL +1.89%) or lululemon athletica (LULU -2.76%) better suits their 2027 goals.

    In a recent development, colgate-Palmolive dominates everyday essentials like toothpaste and pet nutrition, while Lululemon leads the premium athletic wear market. One offers defensive qualities in volatile markets, and the other aims for expansion in international retail. This comparison looks at their growth paths, financial health, and current valuations to help you navigate these two distinct paths.

    Recent findings suggest that colgate-Palmolive reaches consumers in more than 200 countries with a diverse portfolio including oral care, home hygiene, and specialty pet nutrition. In its latest annual report, Walmart (WMT +1.51%) and its affiliates accounted for nearly 11% of total net sales. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk, though the firm continues to expand its presence in emerging markets among consumer staples stocks.

    In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached approximately $21.3 billion, reflecting a growth rate of roughly 5.9%. Net income for the same period was close to $2.1 billion, resulting in a net margin of nearly 9.6%. These results indicate a consistent demand for hygiene and pet health products despite broader economic shifts.

    As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio reached approximately 158.4x, which represents the relationship between its total debt and shareholder equity. The current ratio, measuring the ability to pay short-term debts with current assets, was roughly 0.8x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was close to $3.6 billion.

    In a recent development, lululemon Athletica operates a premium athletic lifestyle business focused on technical apparel, footwear, and accessories. The manufacturer uses an omni-channel approach, selling through over 800 stores and its own digital platforms. The company also uses license and supply arrangements with third parties to enter international markets like the UAE and Israel.

    In the 12 months ended Aug. 2, 2026, revenue reached nearly $11.1 billion, representing a growth rate of approximately 1.7%. Net income for this period was roughly $1.4 billion, resulting in a net margin of nearly 12.8%. The slower revenue growth suggests a period of normalization following years of rapid post-pandemic expansion.

    As of its February 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was nearly 0.4x, showing the company uses relatively little debt compared to its equity. The current ratio was approximately 2.3x, suggesting a strong ability to cover short-term obligations. In the fiscal year ended Feb. 1, 2026, free cash flow reached close to $921.7 million.

    Colgate-Palmolive faces significant exposure to international markets and fluctuations in foreign currency values. The manufacturer deals with intense global competition from traditional rivals like Procter & Gamble (NYSE:PG) and newer private-label manufacturers. It also manages substantial legal uncertainty regarding ongoing talc-related litigation and operational risks from potential supply chain disruptions.

    Industry observers note that lululemon Athletica manages heightened competition in the athletic apparel market, especially from imitation products. The tech giant is vulnerable to supply chain disruptions because its manufacturing and fabric sourcing are concentrated in the APAC region. Additionally, it faces reputational risks from pending securities class action lawsuits and sensitivity to changes in U.S. tariff policy.

    Lululemon Athletica appears significantly cheaper than its peer, as it carries a lower Forward P/E and a lower P/S ratio, which measures sales over the past twelve months.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    I'd go with Colgate-Palmolive. It sells everyday products around the world and has raised its dividend for 63 straight years, a record built on things people buy in any economy. It holds the biggest share of the world's toothpaste market, and its Hill's pet food brand adds a second source of growth.

    Recent findings suggest that last quarter, sales grew in nearly every region, emerging markets like India and Brazil led the way, and management raised its profit outlook. Costs are rising and U.S. shoppers are cautious, but those pressures are hitting the whole industry, and the rest of Colgate's business is still growing.

But sales are shrinking, with North American shoppers buying less at existing stores, and the company cut its full-year outlook in its latest report.     💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that hilton is making a massive play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort.
    • The resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R.
    • Room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that hilton is making a massive play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort. The massive 1,000-room property — which underwent an $80 million renovation before opening under the Signia Hilton brand in May 2026 — sits on the beach in Hollywood, Florida, just outside of Fort Lauderdale.

    The resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R. The main downside: The location isn’t great if your trip primarily revolves around off-property excursions, dining and nightlife.

    Room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable. There’s also a resort fee of $59 per night — but Hilton waives that when you book using Hilton points.

    Hilton covered the cost of my stay for two nights, but the opinions in this review are my own. Here’s what guests can expect at this oceanfront resort.

    Since the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort is part of Hilton Honors, there are several ways to book a stay there.

    If you’re using Hilton points, expect to pay 70,000 to 80,000 points a night when standard rooms are available. Hilton elite status — a benefit you can earn by holding any Hilton Honors credit card — gets you the fifth-night-free perk, where you stay for at least five nights but pay for four when booking with points.

    For example, if you were to stay five nights at 80,000 points a night, you’d pay 320,000 points total, bringing down your average nightly rate to 64,000 points.

    You can also book using Hilton’s generous free night certificates, which can be used at almost any property in the portfolio. If you hold the Hilton Honors American Express Aspire Card, you automatically get a certificate each year. It’s also possible to earn certificates through reaching spending thresholds on the card and on the Hilton Honors American Express Surpass® Card. Terms apply.

    Make sure to check the cash rate against the points rate to make sure you’re getting good value from your redemption. NerdWallet values Hilton points at 0.4 cent apiece.

    In a recent development, for cash bookings of two nights or more, you might consider using The Hotel Collection via American Express’ travel portal for eligible cardholders. Eligible bookings come with benefits like a $100 property credit and other amenities subject to availability, including a room upgrade, early check-in and late checkout.

    Keep in mind that third-party bookings typically don’t earn Hilton points or count toward elite status qualification.

    It’s hard to miss the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort, with its signature H-shaped facade and sleek white-and-glass exterior.

    Stepping into the hotel, I was immediately struck by the lush greenery filling the entrance and indoor courtyard. The grand lobby has soaring glass ceilings, giving the space a greenhouse feel, although the strong air conditioning keeps you cool.

    Sources indicate that despite its massive size, it doesn’t have a sprawling layout, which I appreciated. Everything is close together, and you can walk from the check-in counter to any of the indoor restaurants in under a minute.

    According to recent reports, I stayed in an oceanfront suite with a balcony, which was spacious and had a fun beachy vibe. To get to the rooms, you’ll need to use either the north or south tower elevator banks.

    In the living room, there was a large sitting area featuring a TV, a couch, an accent chair and a four-person high-top table.

    Although I didn’t spend too much time on the balcony — the October balminess was a bit too much for me — I enjoyed stepping out each morning to admire the view.

    The bedroom had a king bed with extremely comfortable bedding and an oversized chair that was a great spot to relax and read a book by the window.

    The bathroom was spacious, featuring a shower and a separate tub (something every room has).

    Even the standard room I toured felt roomy. I liked that it shared similar elements with the suite, including the oversized lounge chair.

    This is what you’d normally get when booking a room at the cheapest points price.

    Sources indicate that there are several dining venues on the property, ranging from a grab-and-go cafe to a high-end steakhouse. It is a luxury resort, so expect the prices to reflect that.

    Sources indicate that for breakfast, you can head to Palmea Kitchen, which is also open for lunch. I had the breakfast buffet, which offered a nice spread of classics, from hot food items and pastries to cold cuts and smoked salmon.

    It has been revealed that if you don’t have time for a sit-down breakfast, you can head next door to The Press, which offers made-to-order and grab-and-go food options throughout the day. You can also get smoothies, juices, snacks, pastries and other sweet treats.

    The Canteen is another grab-and-go option that also sells snacks, drinks, souvenirs and sundries, similar to a convenience store.

    Sources indicate that for lunch and dinner, try Solara. It doesn’t have a traditional restaurant feel, as it’s mostly an indoor-outdoor bar space. One side connects to the lobby, while the other side faces the Solara adults-only pool.

    It serves a lunch menu, as well as a substantial bar food menu that’s available late into the night.

    You can also eat at Playa Beach Bar & Grill, a beachside restaurant serving Latin-inspired cuisine. I enjoyed spending a lazy lunch there and watching the waves crash onto the shore.

    For a fancy sit-down dinner, go to Diplomat Prime, the property’s steakhouse. We had a group dinner at the restaurant, and the meats were, of course, the highlight. But don’t sleep on the seafood, which was also delicious.

    In a recent development, one of the best parts of the Dip, as it’s affectionately known, is its location right on the beach. Guests can access the stretch of beach directly adjacent to the property. But it’s not a private beach, so you might encounter crowds.

    I didn’t spend any time on the beach itself — it was extremely windy while I was there — but the hotel’s resort fee includes amenities like a beach lounge (umbrella not included), a daily one-hour kayak or paddleboard rental, and beachfront yoga classes.

    If you don’t want to get sand everywhere, you can head to one of the three pool options: the adults-only Solara pool, the family-friendly lagoon pool and the Verandah Social Club for those 21 and older (requires paid access).

    In a recent development, the family-friendly lagoon spans the length of the property and runs beneath the Solara pool. It also has its own hot tub.

    I spent an afternoon in a cabana at the Verandah Social Club, which has some smaller plunge pools and a hot tub.

    I appreciated the attentive service from the staff there, who constantly checked on whether guests needed anything.

    If you’re looking for other ways to stay active, head to the two-story fitness center, featuring a variety of equipment like free weights, exercise bikes, a rowing machine and treadmills.

    Next door, you’ll find the spa and wellness center. I had a relaxing massage that incorporated hot stones and aromatherapy.

    The locker rooms come with a sauna and steam room, although I wished there were more amenities like a hot tub and cold plunge.

    It has been revealed that one of the resort fee inclusions is complimentary high-intensity interval training workout classes at the gym across the street. I signed up for an early morning class. The instructor was friendly, and it was a great way to start my day.

    Other amenities include a complimentary one-hour e-bike rental each day, as well as a kids’ club with various activities (but drop-off fees apply).

    I had a fantastic stay at this resort, but I’d recommend it for a specific traveler.

    If you’re planning to stay on-property your entire trip, it’s a great option. That’s probably why it’s such a popular convention hotel, since everything you need is easily accessible.

    I loved the hotel’s design, including the jungle-like atmosphere in the lobby, and I found the dining options to be tasty, albeit pricey.

    But if your trip revolves around visiting Miami attractions, you’ll likely want to stay closer to the action.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that shares of Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) fell 14% on Friday afternoon, to less than $126, after Reuters reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating the chipmaker's accounting.
    • Recent findings suggest that zoom out and the damage is even bigger.
    • Here's what we know, and what investors should make of it.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jonathan Ponciano – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:07PM EST.

    Nvidia's terrible month just got worse.

    Industry observers note that shares of Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) fell 14% on Friday afternoon, to less than $126, after Reuters reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating the chipmaker's accounting. The drop erased roughly $491 billion in market value in a single session, taking Nvidia from about $3.52 trillion to about $3.03 trillion.

    Recent findings suggest that zoom out and the damage is even bigger. Nvidia closed at a record $239.24 on Oct. 6. At Friday's price, the stock is down about 48% from that high, and the organization has lost about $2.7 trillion in value in just six weeks.

    Here's what we know, and what investors should make of it.

    It has been revealed that the Wall Street Journal first reported on Tuesday that the SEC was investigating Nvidia but couldn't say what the probe was about. On Friday, Reuters, citing two people briefed on the matter, reported that the agency's enforcement staff are examining potential accounting problems at the company.

    It has been revealed that many questions remain unanswered. Reuters couldn't determine when the inquiry began or which accounting practices are under review. The SEC declined to comment, and Nvidia didn't immediately respond. Keep in mind that the SEC investigates plenty of companies that are never charged with anything.

    The stock was already having a bad day before the report: shares were down more than 6% earlier in the session amid a broad sell-off in AI stocks.

    According to recent reports, the probe adds to a pile of problems. Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on Nov. 11 following revelations about his personal relationships, including with a woman U.S. authorities suspect of spying for China, which China denies. The Justice Department is also reviewing Nvidia's planned $12.9 billion purchase of Hugging Face, according to Reuters.

    According to recent reports, two areas could draw scrutiny. The first is how Nvidia reports where its sales come from. The firm breaks out revenue by where customers are headquartered, rather than where they're billed. On that basis, about 63% of last quarter's revenue came from U.S.-based customers. The Financial Times has reported that Nvidia made the switch as sales billed to Singapore approached half of its total, a bad look with Southeast Asia having become a hub for chips smuggled into China.

    Recent findings suggest that the second is how Nvidia helps its customers pay for its chips. On Tuesday's earnings call, interim CEO Colette Kress said Nvidia's guarantees totaled $118 billion at the end of the quarter, including $105 billion of credit support tied to a single data center campus. These guarantees are the kind of disclosure the SEC is watching closely at AI companies. When a chipmaker helps fund the projects that buy its chips, it's harder to tell how much demand would exist on its own.

    None of this has shown up in the numbers yet. Nvidia's revenue jumped 103% to $115.8 billion last quarter, and the firm expects about $130 billion this quarter. Management even raised its growth forecast for next fiscal year to about 75%. At about $126, the stock trades at roughly 12 times last quarter's adjusted earnings of $2.68 per share on an annualized basis, cheap for a company growing this fast.

    According to recent reports, but cheap can get cheaper. Accounting questions hit at the heart of what investors pay for: trust in the numbers. Until Nvidia names a permanent CEO and the SEC's focus becomes clearer, the stock could stay volatile, even after a 48% drop.

    For long-term investors who already own Nvidia, there's no need to panic-sell on a report about an investigation. For anyone thinking of buying, it's smarter to wait for more clarity, or to build a position slowly, than to bet that the worst is over. There are plenty of other semiconductor stocks without a cloud of investigations hanging over them.

    Marvell Reports Dec. 1. History Notes What Its Stock Usually Does Next.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Marvell Technology ›.
    • Marvell Technology (MRVL -11.69%) will release results for its fiscal third quarter of 2027 (the period ended Oct.
    • The chipmaker's stock comes into the report at around $138 as I write, off about 56% from its June 4 record close of $316.43.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:23PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Marvell Technology ›.

    Marvell Technology (MRVL -11.69%) will release results for its fiscal third quarter of 2027 (the period ended Oct. 31, 2026) on Tuesday, Dec. 1, with a conference call at 1:30 p.m. Pacific time.

    The chipmaker's stock comes into the report at around $138 as I write, off about 56% from its June 4 record close of $316.43. And most of that drop is recent. Marvell shares ended Oct. 28 at around $252, the last trading day before speculation started about a deal for optical parts maker Lumentum Holdings.

    Industry observers note that on Nov. 2, the two companies announced an all-stock deal. After it closes, Marvell's current shareholders will own around two-thirds of the combined firm. The growth stock is down about 45% from that Oct. 28 close.

    The Dec. 1 report will be Marvell's first full quarterly patch since it agreed to buy Lumentum. And if the past three years are any guide, the shares might make a big move the day after.

    Recent findings suggest that matt Murphy. Image source: Getty Images.

    It has been revealed that marvell reports after the market closes, so the reaction indicates up in the next day's trading. Here are its last 12 reports, the stock's close-to-close move the next day, and the revenue growth management guided for the following quarter over the quarter just reported.

    Data source: Yahoo Finance and Marvell. Calculations by author.

    Shares dropped the next day seven times and climbed five times.

    And the moves were substantial either way. The average swing was around 12%, and seven of the 12 moves topped 10%.

    Interestingly, the quarters themselves were almost never to blame. In all 12 reports, Marvell's revenue came in above the midpoint of its guidance.

    It has been revealed that I think the outlook mattered more. In the six reports in which management guided to next-quarter revenue growth of 6% or lower (with one guide for a decline), the stock fell the next day five times, with an average drop of around 9%.

    In the six where it guided for about 8% or more, shares climbed four times, with an average gain of about 6%.

    But six reports on either side doesn't prove much, and the pattern has a clear exception. In August 2026, management guided to third-quarter revenue of $3.15 billion, up 15% from the second quarter's $2.74 billion, the second-largest increase in the table. The stock still dropped 10% the next day.

    A possible reason is that expectations had risen with the tech organization's share price, which had more than tripled since the March 2026 report.

    This time, the quarter itself could hold even less surprise than normal. When it declared the Lumentum deal on Nov. 2, Marvell noted preliminary third-quarter revenue was in line with its guidance. It kept the $3.15 billion midpoint and tightened the range to plus or minus 2%.

    According to recent reports, that puts the focus on the fiscal fourth quarter, and the bar is high for a chipmaker helped by demand for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure. Marvell's revenue climbed 22% year over year in the final quarter of fiscal 2026. Growth then rose to 28% and 37% in the first two quarters of fiscal 2027. And the $3.15 billion third-quarter midpoint means growth of around 52%, an acceleration for a third straight quarter.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    "[W]e expect our revenue growth to accelerate further through the remainder of fiscal 2027," Marvell CEO Matt Murphy stated in the company's fiscal second-quarter earnings release.

    For growth to keep accelerating in the fiscal fourth quarter, revenue would have to exceed $3.4 billion, or about 7% above the third-quarter midpoint. In other words, a guide that just keeps pace with the third quarter might land right around the line that has split the stock's past reactions.

    Recent findings suggest that in the end, I'd expect a big move on Dec. 2 either way, and a down day has been a bit more common than an up day. But I wouldn't read much into one day's move when the Lumentum deal isn't expected to close until the first half of 2028.

    Sources indicate that personally, I'd pay more attention to the size of the fourth-quarter guide than to the stock's reaction to it. Shares trade at around 20 times the earnings analysts expect for fiscal 2028, a price that seems reasonable if growth continues to accelerate. And if shares drop again on a guide that still shows accelerating growth, I think the lower price might be worth considering for investors who can ride out more swings like these.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The stock market continues to grapple with volatility amid geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and concerns about the sustainability of the AI boom. Given this uncertainty, investors looking for steady income can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios.

    Tracking the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick the right dividend stocks, as these experts assign their ratings after an in-depth analysis of a manufacturer's financials and ability to pay dividends consistently.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Downstream energy organization Phillips 66 (PSX) is this week's first dividend pick. With a quarterly dividend $1.27 per share (annualized dividend of $5.08), PSX offers a yield of 2.25%. The company recently reported solid Q2 earnings, as the Middle East conflict affected global supplies and drove up refining margins.

    Following the Q2 print, TD Cowen analyst Jason Gabelman reiterated a buy rating on Phillips 66 and raised his price target to $255 from $240, reflecting higher 2026 earnings expectations and lower interest expense next year.

    Sources indicate that gabelman highlighted the quarter-over-quarter reduction in Phillips 66's net debt, noting management's optimism at achieving its estimated $15.5 billion net debt target one year ahead of schedule. The 5-star analyst expects the company to end 2026 with a net debt of $14.6 billion.

    "The [balance sheet] improvement could re-establish PSX as a go-to defensive refiner," stated Gabelman.

    Management agreed that PSX's payout ratio lagged year-to-date, but expects buybacks to increase in the second half. Gabelman mentioned Phillps indicated the possibility of a larger dividend hike following an annual increase of 5% over the past two years.

    Gabelman ranks No. 554 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 66% of the time, delivering an average return of 14.9%. See Phillips 66 Statistics on TipRanks.

    Crescent Energy (CRGY) is an exploration and production company with activities focused in the Eagle Ford, Permian and Uinta Basins. Earlier this month, the company reported better-than-expected Q2 earnings and confirmed a quarterly dividend of $0.12 per share, payable on August 31. At an annualized dividend of $0.48 per share, CRGY boasts a dividend yield of about 4%.

    In a recent development, in reaction to Q2 results, Evercore analyst Stephen Richardson reaffirmed a buy rating on Crescent Energy stock with a price target of $18. He noted continued strength in the tech giant's performance, with second-quarter oil production and cash flow surpassing the Street's expectations.

    "CRGY's cash flow exceeded expectations by 10%, reinforcing its trajectory of capital efficiency," said Richardson.

    Recent findings suggest that the 5-star analyst highlighted that Crescent raised its full-year oil production guidance, citing the effective integration of the Vital Energy acquisition. Specifically, Crescent tripled its synergy target from the Vital Energy deal to as much as $300 million, significantly reducing the effective purchase price. This reflects Crescent's solid execution following the acquisition, Richardson noted.

    Additionally, the analyst noted that Crescent's capital spending is and heading toward the lower end of management's prior guidance, indicating disciplined financial controls.

    It has been revealed that richardson ranks No. 579 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 65% of the time, delivering an average return of 12.5%. See Crescent Energy Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    It has been revealed that finally, Viper Energy (VNOM) is effectively controlled by Diamondback Energy. Viper owns and acquires mineral and royalty interests in oil-weighted basins, mainly the Permian in West Texas. Viper recently announced its Q2 2026 results and declared a 32% hike in its base dividend, effective in the third quarter of 2026. The fresh base dividend indicates a 4.5% annualized yield.

    Recent findings suggest that viper also removed its quarterly commitment to return at least 75% of cash available for distribution. The company believes that this move will ensure increased flexibility to make opportunistic share repurchases and pursue accretive mergers and acquisitions.

    Following the Q2 results, TD Cowen analyst Aaron Bilkoski reiterated a buy rating on Viper, slightly raising his price target to $59 from $58. Bilkoski said Viper's solid Q2 performance supports his view that the strength in oil prices and rising operator activity are driving higher production.

    "Viper has delivered, and we forecast will continue to deliver, one of the highest production per share growth profiles in our royalty universe" through the end of 2027, said Bilkoski. He believes Viper deserves a premium valuation, given its above-average growth.

    The 5-star analyst said that while the biggest surprise in the quarter was Viper's revision to its shareholder return framework, he doesn't believe that the move indicates a significant change to its underlying strategy. Under the upcoming framework, a larger portion of excess free cash flow is expected to be allocated to share repurchases than to variable dividends, Bilkoski said.

    Bilkoski ranks No. 719 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Viper Energy Financials on TipRanks.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Atmos Rewards is the airline loyalty program for Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines. One of its newer features is Atmos Communities, which offer additional rewards and benefits tailored to different travel interests.

    There are six communities, including two reserved for Alaska and Hawaii residents. The other four are open to members regardless of where they live. But don’t get caught up in the community names. The best choice for you may depend more on your travel looks than the groupings suggest.

    Here’s how to decide which Atmos Community best fits your travel patterns.

    » Learn more: The guide to Atmos Rewards.

    Atmos Communities are like groups within the Atmos Rewards program that offer additional benefits based on different travel interests.

    They’re free to join for Atmos Rewards members. Four communities are available to all members, while community Club 49 is reserved for Alaska residents and community Huaka’i by Hawaiian is reserved for Hawaii residents.

    In a recent development, you can belong to only one community at a time and switch communities once per calendar year. Consider your upcoming travel plans before choosing.

    Industry observers note that each Atmos Community has a list of 10 destinations where members can earn bonus points and status points. Although the destinations differ by community, the rewards structure is the same.

    According to recent reports, through Dec. 31, 2027, members can earn up to 10,000 bonus points and 10,000 status points by visiting qualifying destinations.

    Here’s how many points you’ll earn as you reach each milestone:.

    Visit one destination, earn 100 status and bonus points.

    Visit two destinations, earn 200 status and bonus points.

    Visit three destinations, earn 300 status and bonus points.

    Visit four destinations, earn 400 status and bonus points.

    Visit five destinations, earn 500 status and bonus points.

    Visit six destinations, earn 750 status and bonus points.

    Visit seven destinations, earn 1,000 status and bonus points.

    Visit eight destinations, earn 1,250 status and bonus points.

    Visit nine destinations, earn 2,500 status and bonus points.

    Visit 10 destinations, earn 3,000 status and bonus points.

    The first member of each community to visit all 10 qualifying destinations during the challenge period will also earn 100,000 bonus points.

    It has been revealed that new lists of qualifying destinations for each community take effect on Jan. 1, 2028.

    Here’s a closer look at the six communities, their benefits and the destinations eligible for bonus points.

    Sources indicate that global Locals is geared toward frequent international travelers. Benefits include:.

    Earn 10% more status points toward Atmos elite status on flights that begin and/or end outside the U.S., including award flights.

    Earn 1 status point for every 25 points transferred to Atmos Rewards from Bilt or Marriott Bonvoy.

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    According to recent reports, through Dec. 31, 2027, these 10 Oneworld Alliance hubs count toward bonus points and status points. Qualifying layovers also count toward the destination challenge, so you don’t necessarily need to make these cities your final stop.

    If you frequently travel internationally or have any upcoming flights through any of these airports, including qualifying layovers, Global Locals might be a fit for you.

    Industry observers note that if you have the Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® credit card, you’ll earn 3 Atmos points per $1 spent on eligible Alaska and Hawaiian Airlines purchases, dining and foreign transactions. The last bonus category can be especially useful for frequent international travelers.

    Sources indicate that this community has a similar setup to Global Locals, but most of its bonus destinations are in the U.S. Here’s what you can get:.

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    Sources indicate that through Dec. 31, 2027, here are the 10 destinations that count toward the bonus:.

    This community would be an excellent choice if your upcoming travels include several of these airports, even if dining isn't the main reason for your trips. If dining out is one of your favorite activities, check out the best credit cards for restaurants.

    Industry observers note that active Escapes focuses on airports in outdoor-oriented destinations that are all in the U.S., save one. Benefits here are:.

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    Industry observers note that through Dec. 31, 2027, here are the 10 destinations that count toward the bonus:.

    While these airports are gateways to national parks and other natural attractions, you don’t have to be an outdoor enthusiast to benefit. Like before, don’t let the heading sway you. Rather, consider the destinations before you decide.

    Families On the Go might appeal to you if you redeem Atmos Rewards for your children. Benefits include:.

    Get 20% of your points back on eligible award flights for kids 12 and under after you complete your trip.

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    Through Dec. 31, 2027, these destinations qualify for bonus points and status points:.

    This community may be especially valuable if you regularly book award flights for children 12 and under. Even if you don't travel with kids, it could be worth considering if its qualifying airports align better with your travel plans than those of other communities.

    Exclusively for Alaska residents, Club 49 offers rewards that are focused on travel to, from and within the state:.

    Two free checked bags when traveling to or from Alaska on Alaska Airlines or Hawaiian Airlines.

    Three free checked bags when traveling within Alaska on Alaska Airlines.

    Two Travel Now discounts per year for 30% off one-way refundable Y-class fares on Alaska Airlines, booked within four days of departure for travel to, from or within Alaska.

    Ship cargo within Alaska for $49 plus tax (weight, size and content limits apply).

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    Baggage benefits don’t combine with other free checked bag allowances, such as those that come with some Alaska credit cards. However, they apply to everyone traveling on the same reservation.

    Sources indicate that through Dec. 31, 2027, here are the 10 destinations that count toward the bonus offers:.

    While this community is only for Alaskans, you might decide one of the other communities more closely matches your travel intends — especially if you already have an Alaska credit card with free baggage benefits. However, if you ship a lot of cargo or think you’ll use the Travel Now discounts, those are special benefits that may sway you to choose Club 49.

    It has been revealed that hawaii residents have their own community just for them: Huaka’i by Hawaiian. It offers benefits focused on interisland travel:.

    Two free checked bags on neighbor island flights on Hawaiian Airlines, including sports equipment like surfboards and golf bags.

    Quarterly fare discounts of 10% off one neighbor island booking, or 20% off for eligible Hawaiian Airlines® World Elite Mastercard® and Atmos™ Rewards Visa® cardholders.

    Earn 50% more points and status points on flights between Hawaiian islands beginning Jan. 1, 2027.

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    The 10 destinations eligible for bonus points through Dec. 31, 2027 are:.

    Sources indicate that seven destinations are in Hawaii, with one on the mainland and two international cities. If you live in Hawaii and like to hop between islands, this community is a strong choice.

    Don’t be persuaded by the names of the communities. Look a little deeper, because there’s a lot of overlap between destination lists. Compare the options against your upcoming travel intends.

    According to recent reports, you can change communities once per calendar year, so you aren’t locked in to your initial choice indefinitely. However, switching communities resets your destination-challenge progress, but you’ll retain any points you’ve already earned.

    If your home airport (or one you visit frequently) is already on a community’s list, you may have an easier time earning points. Also consider whether a particular community benefit, such as free checked bags or points back on award flights for kids, outweighs the destination challenge.

    Industry observers note that finally, pay attention to airport codes. For example, Tokyo’s Narita (NRT) and Haneda (HND) appear on different community lists. New York’s qualifying airport is JFK, while it is DCA in Washington, D.C. If you have a choice between airports, check which one qualifies for your community’s challenge.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.
    • Industry observers note that the Bridgewater Associates founder noted Bessent's proposal to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S.
    • Sources indicate that "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.

    Industry observers note that the Bridgewater Associates founder noted Bessent's proposal to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S. economy. Coupled with the Japanese government reducing its U.S. bond market exposure and surging long-dated American bond yields, Dalio said investors may want to prepare their portfolios for increased risk by owning cryptocurrencies and gold.

    Sources indicate that "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

    Dalio noted that the Treasury Department has "only limited capacity" to buy back bonds. Bessent told CNBC on Thursday that his team was going to "make a market" and that the purchases would likely top $4 billion.

    It has been revealed that the U.S. is spending about 40% more than it's bringing in, resulting in the burgeoning budget deficit, Dalio mentioned. The U.S. budget deficit topped $432 billion in July, but Bessent told CNBC that it's likely peaked under President Donald Trump's administration.

    Sources indicate that bessent said in the interview that a team was looking at ways to shrink spending by hundreds of billions of dollars. But Dalio said there is "very little ability" to do so given that it is either committed or considered essential.

    After years of overspending, Dalio stated total debt now dwarfs what the U.S. brings in each year. If the U.S. government was a business, Dalio said debt service payments would come in at roughly $11 trillion — about 200% of annual revenue.

    Dalio, 77, warned the cost of repaying principal and servicing the debt will only grow over time.

    According to recent reports, to solve this, Dalio mentioned the U.S. needs to carefully employ a three-part strategy to get the budget deficit down to 3% of gross domestic product.

    First, Dalio said the U.S. government needs to reduce its spending. Second, he said tax revenue needs to be raised. Finally, the Latest York native and Harvard Business School alumni said lower interest rates were needed.

    Sources indicate that "All three need to happen concurrently so as to prevent any one from being too large," Dalio said. "If any one is too large, the adjustment will be traumatic.".

    Dalio cautioned against ramming through these adjustments by "force." For instance, "it would be very bad if the Federal Reserve unnaturally forced interest rates down," he remarked.

    In a recent development, dalio said it's important to to take steps now, while the economy is healthy. An economy in recession requires increased government spending, he said.

    In a recent development, dalio remarked the exact timing of a debt crisis can be swayed by variables ranging from military conflict to political change. On its current trajectory, the U.S. could enter such a crisis in as early as one year or as late as five. "My guess, which I suppose will be a bad one, is that it will come in three years, give or take two, if the course we're on is not changed.".

    To prepare, Dalio recommended investors are underweight debt assets, such as bonds.

    As much as 10% to 15% of a portfolio could land in gold, as well as "a bit" of bitcoin, the hedge fund founder said.

    According to recent reports, dalio's post came at the tail end of a volatile week for U.S. financial markets. Rising long-term Treasury yields have pressured stocks, leading the S&P 500 to snap a a three-week-long advance.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Mortgage rates dropped today, but anything above 7% still puts pressure on home buyers’ budgets.
    • It has been revealed that the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.24% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow.
    • According to recent reports, A significant drop is eye-catching, but you should consider mortgage interest rates' overall direction, not just what's going on today.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mortgage rates dropped today, but anything above 7% still puts pressure on home buyers’ budgets.

    It has been revealed that the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.24% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 14 basis points lower than yesterday and three basis points lower than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

    According to recent reports, A significant drop is eye-catching, but you should consider mortgage interest rates' overall direction, not just what's going on today. While the economy never sleeps, markets are closed on the weekends. The rates you see Friday are unlikely to change much (if at all) until Monday.

    Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:.

    » Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    It has been revealed that mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

    Next week, the Nerds are waiting for the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, due out Wednesday. It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. Stubbornly high inflation is a big reason why we’re seeing upward pressure on mortgage rates right now.

    If PCE indicates inflation comes in hotter than expected, mortgage rates could climb as markets anticipate further Fed rate hikes. (An increase to the federal funds rate is already widely expected at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting.) A cooler reading could ease some pressure on mortgage rates for now.

    I’m not getting my hopes up too high for meaningfully lower inflation, though. Last week's Producer Price Index showed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its fastest pace in four years. Wholesale inflation measures the price businesses pay for things. When businesses’ costs go up, they could pass those along to consumers in the form of higher prices — keeping the flames of inflation alive.

    Whether Wednesday's PCE brings relief or another helping of bad inflation news, we'll know before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

    Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

    With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.74% or higher.

    Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

    If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

    Industry observers note that » Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

    Recent findings suggest that if the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

    NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a latest home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

    » Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis.

    According to recent reports, if you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

    Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

    Recent findings suggest that 🤓 Nerdy Reminder: Rates can change daily, and even hourly. If you’re happy with the deal you have, it’s okay to commit.

    The rate you see advertised is a sample rate — usually for a borrower with perfect credit, making a big down payment, and paying for mortgage points. That won't match every buyer's circumstances.

    In addition to market factors outside of your control, your customized quote depends on your:.

    Even two people with similar credit scores might get different rates, depending on their overall financial profiles.

    Cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD) is this week's first stock pick. The company is scheduled to announce fiscal second-quarter results on August 26.

    In a recent development, the 5-star analyst's optimism is backed by continued strength in Falcon Flex adoption and encouraging large deal activity. Siddiqui also cited continued momentum across emerging products. With the FY27 outlook assuming persistent strength in CrowdStrike's net new annual recurring revenue (ARR), Siddiqui is more focused on the longevity of key growth catalysts such as Falcon Flex adoption, platform consolidation and AI-led demand.

    The analyst highlighted that talks with partners were encouraging, with pipeline generation and momentum in large deals remaining healthy in the fiscal second quarter despite tough, year-over-year comparisons.

    "We continue to view CrowdStrike as one of the primary beneficiaries of platform consolidation, though we expect investors to remain focused on competitive dynamics and whether current growth levels represent a latest baseline or a period of demand acceleration," the analyst noted.

    Industry observers note that siddiqui ranks No. 226 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 80% of the time, delivering an average return of about 40%. See CrowdStrike Financials on TipRanks.

    The 5-star analyst contends that while Dell's AI compute segment is getting investors' attention, the manufacturer's Storage business is underappreciated and well-positioned to drive revenue and profit acceleration. Daryanani expects the storage business to see higher demand once enterprises start to bring workload back on-premises.

    It has been revealed that the analyst highlighted that Dell's Storage business, estimated to account for only 10% of FY27 revenue, is one of the factors that could help improve profit margins, given its higher profitability compared to AI servers. Daryanani estimates that the Storage business's operating margin is right now in the low-20% range, while margins for the AI server and traditional server businesses are in the mid-single-digit and mid-teens range, respectively.

    Overall, Daryanani views the Storage business as an important catalyst for three reasons: Dell has one of the broadest storage portfolios in the industry; Storage has a significantly higher margin profile than AI servers; and the shift toward proprietary, software-defined storage and AI-focused platforms.

    "We think DELL's storage business is becoming increasingly strategic as AI infrastructure deployments move beyond GPU procurement and toward full stack + AI-ready architectures," stated Daryanani.

    Daryanani ranks No. 19 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 71% of the time, delivering an average return of 38.70%. See Dell Technologies Statistics on TipRanks.

    Sources indicate that sanDisk (SNDK) is benefiting from AI-driven demand for its memory and storage products. Following the organization's 2026 Investor Day event, J.P. Morgan analyst Harlan Sur resumed research coverage of SNDK with a buy rating (it was earlier, "Not Rated") and a price target of $2,250.

    The 5-star analyst believes SanDisk is well-positioned to capitalize on a structural inflection reached in NAND demand, driven by strong growth in AI inference. Sur's bullishness is based on three key factors.

    Sources indicate that first, Sur believes that SanDisk's New Business Model (NBM) framework (or long-term agreements) has enhanced its margin profile and reduced cyclicality. SNDK's eight signed NBMs represent a total contract value of $94 billion and a gross margin of about 80%, even at the floor pricing.

    Second, Sur highlighted the growing NAND market and expects the total addressable market to surge from about $70 billion in calendar year 2025 to over $300 billion in 2026 and about $500 billion in 2027. Importantly, the analyst noted that data centers are the largest driver of NAND growth, as hyperscalers increasingly deploy flash for AI inference workloads.

The tech giant's BiCS10 technology is sampling ahead of schedule and has 65% more bits per wafer than BiCS8, the analyst said. Also, Sur expects SanDisk's High Bandwidth Flash to become a differentiated memory platform for AI inference.

    College Scholarship Breakdown: Types, Sponsors and Eligibility at a Glance

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1389 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college.
    • In a recent development, before you go searching for a scholarship, it's notable to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding.
    • According to recent reports, scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college. You can learn about scholarships in a variety of ways, but looking through an online database of available scholarships — the most common way — can be overwhelming.

    In a recent development, before you go searching for a scholarship, it's notable to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding. Here’s what you need to know about scholarships to decide which ones are best for you.

    According to recent reports, scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies. None is better than the other when it comes to awarding funds.

    Nonprofit organizations and clubs that are looking for students either majoring in or researching certain fields, or who have experience volunteering in a specific field.

    Companies that want to support all students or only fund those majoring in a field that relates to the companies’ industries.

    Financial institutions, such as banks or credit unions, that want to support their community or their members.

    Individuals or families that are funding private scholarships, usually in memory of a loved one.

    Universities and colleges that are offering funds to students who attend their campuses.

    Research organizations that want to fund students who will research in their areas of interest and further their causes.

    These scholarships generally are provided by local, state or federal government agencies for a variety of reasons. Despite being funded by a government agency, the scholarships do not require you to pay back the money — unlike federal student loans.

    According to recent reports, some scholarships pay for anything related to college expenses, including tuition, room and board, books and supplies, and more. Other scholarships limit what you can pay for with the funds, such as only tuition or tuition along with books. It’s important to look at this restriction when applying for scholarships to ensure the funds will go toward what you need to cover.

    Merit scholarships require you to show excellence or achievements in your schoolwork, through talents and abilities, and even leadership or service work. Because these types of awards can be highly competitive, merit scholarships might require more than just achievements, such as volunteer or leadership experience. This means merit-based scholarships can overlap with other types of scholarship categories. Here are some examples of merit-based scholarships:.

    According to recent reports, merit scholarships often require you to have earned a minimum grade point average (GPA). The minimum GPA depends on the scholarship but often ranges from 2.0 to 4.0, with more competitive scholarships usually requiring higher GPAs. Scholarships with lower GPA minimums are more likely to consider additional factors, such as financial need.

    Some merit scholarships might require a minimum ACT or SAT score instead of a GPA — or in addition to a minimum GPA.

    Merit scholarships might also require applicants to have participated in activities outside of their schoolwork. This is common for scholarships that require membership in a certain group or organization. For example, membership in agricultural clubs, such as 4-H or FFA, and scouting groups, such as the National Eagle Scout Association, appear in scholarship requirements.

    Some scholarships emphasize volunteering or community service and only consider applicants who have that experience. Applications vary in how detailed their requirements can be. Some scholarships want only a general description of where and how you’ve volunteered, and others might require experience with a service project that indicates more leadership experience or time volunteering with a certain type of organization.

    Scholarships that are awarded to students who can’t afford college are called need-based scholarships.

    Sources indicate that unmet financial need is the difference between what it will cost you to attend college and what you can afford to pay. Because calculating how much you can afford is a complicated process, many scholarships refer to your FAFSA to document your financial need.

    It has been revealed that some scholarship requirements may be as straightforward as demonstrating that you have financial need, but some scholarships might have income limits. However, income restrictions are less common.

    Industry observers note that athletic scholarships are for — you guessed it — athletes. They are usually offered by colleges and universities to recruit athletes onto their collegiate teams and can be competitive. Which sports have scholarships available and the scholarship amounts vary by college.

    Sources indicate that even though the main criterion for an athletic scholarship is being good at your sport, you’ll likely still need to show that you can keep up with your schoolwork. Most athletic scholarships require students to earn a minimum GPA or test scores to remain eligible while they’re in college.

    Some scholarships are designated for students majoring in a general field, such as science or education, but others can be for very specific areas of study. For example, a scholarship for students majoring in a natural resource field could include majors in biology, ecology, wildlife biology, conservation education, forestry, soils and hydrology. However, a stricter scholarship might state that students have to major in more specific topics, such as biochemistry or microbial ecology.

    It has been revealed that scholarships are available for active and former members of the military and members of their families. In addition to federal funds available for veterans to attend college, private organizations and some universities have scholarships for veterans to offset the cost of a degree.

    Which family members can apply for funds depends on the individual scholarship. For example, some scholarships extend to children or spouses of veterans, but some go as far in a family tree as great-grandchildren.

    In a recent development, veteran- and military-focused scholarships might require that applicants or their family members enlisted in a certain branch, served during a particular time or conflict, or meet a certain rank or status such as receiving disability. Scholarships might also require that the applicant be a wartime veteran or family member of a wartime veteran; not all veterans meet this status.

    Industry observers note that scholarships are also awarded to people who identify with a certain group. Common examples of identity-based scholarships include those for people who have disabilities, belong to certain ethnic or religious groups, identify as LGBTQIA+ or are first-generation students. Some identity-based scholarships require applicants to meet several criteria, such as belonging to more than one identity group.

    Outside of what would be considered standard DEI groups, there are scholarships for applicants who identify with less common groups, such as veganism, homelessness and model railroad builders.

    The best scholarships for you depend on your situation. For example, if you are a skilled athlete with a good academic record, going for an athletic scholarship might give you the most funding. On the other hand, if you’re going to research a topic that isn’t common, looking for scholarships that support your research topic might be your best bet because competition could be lower.

    Good tactics to figure out which scholarships are worth your time include:.

    Industry observers note that think of the skills, talents, experience and identities that are unique to you. For example, being a child of a veteran immediately qualifies you for scholarships with fewer applicants than scholarships open to everyone. Likewise, if you embrace a certain ethnicity, identify with a specific group or have experience with a type of work, you might qualify for scholarships that appreciate and recognize those attributes more than the average scholarship.

    It has been revealed that apply if you think you're eligible. Don’t apply to just a few scholarships and hope you get them. Instead, apply for as many scholarships as you can and for which you’re eligible. This increases your chances of receiving funds. Even small scholarships can make a big impact when you add several of them together.

    Understand how you can use the money. If you already have a scholarship that covers only books, applying for the same type of scholarship isn’t helpful if you don’t need the extra funds. Instead, look for scholarships that cover the costs you have remaining.

    Sources indicate that not sure where to look? Our sister site Scholarships360.org provides students with vetted scholarship opportunities. That would be a good place to start.

    Addas a preferred source on Google.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The debasement trade is gaining new traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.

    In a recent development, the conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S. dollar and Treasury debt in the face of ballooning government spending. Those fears reached a fever pitch last week before, and after, the Treasury Department's unusual step of increasing debt buybacks under Secretary Scott Bessent.

    "The size of the Treasury purchases announced so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," stated Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.

    Gold touched three-month highs Monday, building on last week's advance of more than 5%. The yellow metal has climbed for five straight weeks and in August is on track for its biggest monthly rise since 1999.

    In a recent development, bitcoin added 2% Monday, to the highest since May. Last week, the digital currency soared 22%, its biggest three-day rally since 2023. Overnight Tuesday, the crypto touched $80,000.

    Conversely, investors fled the dollar.

    The U.S. dollar index, which tracks the dollar against six other leading currencies, hit three-month lows last week and recorded its third down week in the last four. The index was little changed on Monday as investors expressed little appetite to bid up the greenback.

    The Treasury Department remarked last week that it would double the maximum size of its bond buyback, to at least $4 billion from $2 billion. Two senior Treasury officials told CNBC Monday that the department could use its General Account to help fund the aims.

    In a recent development, last week's announcement followed news that the monthly U.S. budget deficit in July reached a five-year high and came at the same time as total federal government debt topped $40 trillion. Bessent told CNBC last week that he wields a "substantial toolkit" to calm the government bond market amid concerns about the government's financial health.

    Recent findings suggest that long-dated U.S. Treasury yields surged last week, at one point sending the 30-year yield to almost a 20-year high of 5.34%, up from 4.82% in late June. Yields dipped and then rebounded in the wake of the Treasury buyback move, a signal that bond investors believed Bessent's moves were inadequate.

    It has been revealed that "Markets are saying something," the billionaire philanthropist and former energy trader John Arnold mentioned in a Friday post on X. The weaker dollar, lower Treasury prices and strengthening hard assets, are "all part of the debasement trade," he wrote.

    The Treasury's moves could aid the bond market, but also translate into outsized pain for the dollar, according to Nohshad Shah, Citadel Securities' head of fixed income sales for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

    The stakes are high for monetary policymakers, as a weaker greenback can ease financial conditions, Shah said. U.S. inflation — above the Federal Reserve's 2% target for five years — could worsen.

    In a recent development, the Fed might need to hike interest rates in response, Shah noted. Fed funds futures reflect about a 56% chance the central bank raises borrowing costs at its October meeting, up more than seven percentage points from a week ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

    It has been revealed that "The bond market's message is straightforward: fiscal or monetary policy should be tighter," Shah mentioned in a Monday note. "Households may ultimately pay for policymakers' unwillingness to fix the roof whilst the sun is shining.".

    Coltman at 21Shares noted the appetite for alternative stores of value also stems from mounting geopolitical tension. The U.S. on Monday rolled out a global sanctions program focused on segregating Iran from the global economy, days after slapping 50% tariffs on billions of dollars in Canadian exports.

    Still, assets that would benefit from a debasement trade have recently received votes of confidence on Wall Street.

    It has been revealed that deutsche Bank analyst Michael Hsueh said in a Monday note that gold could surpass his target price of $4,800 an ounce. Already, that level suggests the precious metal only need to rise another 3% or so from where it closed on Friday. "We see the Treasury policy change as underlining the gold constructive view," Hsueh said.

    Recent findings suggest that billionaire investor Ray Dalio recommended investors remain overweight gold and bitcoin ahead of what he warned could become a debt crisis in the U.S. as a result of unchecked government spending. Gold could account for as much as 15% of a model portfolio, the Bridgewater Associates founder said.

    "The government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote on LinkedIn Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

    Others are less sure, devaluing the notion of a debasement trade.

    It's probably too early to endorse the idea unless it's clear that the Fed will go along with the Treasury Department, said Alexander Lis, investing chief at Social Discovery Ventures.
