    #62293. When To End A Technology Pilot: 19 Warning Signs

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1314 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    When To End A Technology Pilot: 19 Warning Signs

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1314 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Technology pilots give organizations an opportunity to test newly introduced solutions on a limited scale, evaluate their potential and identify challenges before committing to a broader rollout.
    • According to recent reports, for tech leaders, the challenge is distinguishing between setbacks that can be addressed by adjusting a pilot’s scope or timeline and more fundamental concerns that call its viability into question.
    • In a recent development, A pilot without success criteria is not a pilot.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Technology pilots give organizations an opportunity to test newly introduced solutions on a limited scale, evaluate their potential and identify challenges before committing to a broader rollout. But not every pilot warrants further investment, and knowing when to end one can be just as important as knowing when to expand it.

    According to recent reports, for tech leaders, the challenge is distinguishing between setbacks that can be addressed by adjusting a pilot’s scope or timeline and more fundamental concerns that call its viability into question. Below, members of Forbes Technology Council share warning signs that indicate it’s time to end a technology pilot rather than extend it, redesign it or move it into production.

    In a recent development, A pilot without success criteria is not a pilot. Defining boundaries and expectations, and, importantly, being transparent, are critical to a pilot’s success. Users should also share any uncertainty during the pilot instead of waiting for it to pivot or improve. - Arunava Sen, Tata Communications America Inc.

    According to recent reports, A clear sign is when the pilot team cannot tell you what the technology accessed, what decisions it made, or what data it touched. If you cannot answer those questions in a controlled environment (test group), you will not answer them in production. - Michael Nicosia, Salt Security.

    Sources indicate that forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    According to recent reports, one sign a technology pilot shouldn’t progress doesn’t involve the fresh tech itself but the tools teams already work with. If teams are working in siloed workflows with tools that don’t collaborate with one another, introducing new technology can drive up costs, increase complexity and hurt productivity. Connected tools and workflows are integral to the success of any new tech deployment. - Usman Shuja, Bluebeam.

    Sources indicate that end a pilot when its success depends on hand-curated data that won’t exist in production. If someone cleaned the dataset, resolved definitions and fixed edge cases for the pilot, and no one owns doing that at scale in production, extending or redesigning the product in production won’t help. In many cases, technology isn’t the problem; the foundation is. Ask not whether the pilot worked, but what it worked on. - Prakash Reddy, Okta.

    If the pilot only works while its champion is in the room or while the vendor quietly does manual work behind the scenes, you’ve tested enthusiasm, not technology. Hand it to a team that didn’t build it for 30 days. If results collapse, you’d be pushing a dependency into production, not a tool. End it and keep the learnings. - Damian Wasserman, BEON.tech.

    When the team stops asking what we learned and starts asking when we get to stop, that’s the sign. A pilot without defined success criteria is avoidance. If you can’t name the specific business result it was supposed to prove or disprove, extending it won’t help. End it, define the outcome you actually need, and redesign around that from the start. - Ali Alkhafaji, APPLY.

    Organizations should end a technology pilot when they have full visibility of the tool’s usage and cost metrics but still cannot connect either to a meaningful business outcome. Adoption alone is not enough without a clear path to measurable value, and extending the pilot risks turning experimentation into ongoing spend without a business case. - Conal Gallagher, Flexera.

    A clear sign is when the people who were supposed to benefit stop asking about it. Pilots drag on because the sponsors like the idea, not because users need it. If the pilot group has quietly gone back to their old way of working and nobody complains when the tool goes down, there’s nothing to extend. Name the lesson, thank the team and end it. - Hastimal Jangid, Coozmoo Digital Solutions, Inc.

    A pilot should be reconsidered when it performs well in a demo but can’t prove that it solves a real business problem. AI makes it easy to add capabilities, but more features don’t always mean more value. Teams need clear measures of success and feedback loops to understand what’s working and what’s not before investing further. - Tony Grout, M-Files.

    It has been revealed that A clear sign to end a technology pilot is when it repeatedly fails to demonstrate measurable business value despite validated assumptions and reasonable adjustments. If the solution cannot deliver meaningful ROI, operational efficiency or strategic impact, extending it only increases sunk costs. Strong leadership means knowing when to stop, not just when to scale. - Kameshwar Singh, Cohesity.

    End a pilot if no effort was spent defining the vision and how value will be realized at scale. That’s like building a bridge from both ends without deciding where it should meet. - Venky Ramesh, LatentView Analytics.

    A pilot should end when success depends on conditions that production will never have: handpicked data, expert users, manual fixes, privileged integrations or constant vendor support. If removing that scaffolding collapses the value case, extending the pilot only perfects the illusion. The real test is not, “Does it work?” but, “Does it still create measurable value when exposed to ordinary users, messy data, real constraints and an ordinary day?” - Nicola Sfondrini, PWC.

    End a pilot when making the technology operable, reliable and governable outweighs its business value. If protecting sensitive data, maintaining an audit trail and providing human oversight would cost more than the expected benefit, extending that particular pilot needs a stronger business case than the time and money already invested. - Brian Stimpfl, S-Docs.

    It has been revealed that end a pilot when the evidence invalidates its core business premise. If customers can complete the workflow but gain no meaningful time, cost or quality improvement over the current process, more engineering won’t create demand. Define that minimum benefit before launch, test it with real users, and stop when it remains out of reach. - Irina Shymko, Langate Software.

    It has been revealed that end the pilot when the team cannot define a credible path from the experiment to a measurable business outcome. If success still depends on vague future improvements, heroic manual support or assumptions the pilot was supposed to validate, extending it usually just delays the decision. - Dhyey Mavani, Abridge.

    A pilot should end when the team cannot explain what upcoming evidence another extension will produce. Every extra week should answer a specific open question about value, risk, adoption, cost or scale. Once the remaining time is only keeping the pilot alive, the experiment has already delivered its answer. - Sibasis Padhi, Walmart Inc.

    Industry observers note that I would end a pilot when it successfully completes individual tasks but repeatedly fails to deliver the full business outcome. Often, the underlying concern is the absence of a clear decision model for handling exceptions, approvals or unresolved work across teams. If nobody can authorize what happens next, scaling the technology only scales the problem. - Vamshi Noothi, Cisco.

    A pilot should be ended if nobody uses it unless someone reminds them. A pilot that only stays alive while its sponsor keeps pushing won’t survive production, and extending it just postpones that answer. Software nobody uses isn’t free; it still costs money to run, maintain and support. End it, write down what you learned about the problem, and put the team on something people actually want. - Jeremy Suriel, Kustomer.

    According to recent reports, A clear sign to end a technology pilot is when no business owner is willing to take responsibility for implementation. Even if the technology performs well, success requires business ownership, accountability and commitment to change. Without a sponsor willing to champion the solution, allocate resources and own the outcomes, extending the pilot is unlikely to deliver value. Technology cannot create lasting benefits without clear business ownership. - Eranda Maldeniya, Enterprise Analytics.

    • By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 5:29PM EST.
    • Choosing between these specialized AI plays requires balancing high-stakes government work against commercial data engineering growth.
    • Sources indicate that bigBear.ai provides complex decision intelligence tools for federal and defense agencies, while Innodata helps major tech firms train generative AI systems.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 5:29PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than BigBear.ai ›.

    Choosing between these specialized AI plays requires balancing high-stakes government work against commercial data engineering growth. Investors must decide if BigBear.ai (BBAI -8.67%) or Innodata (INOD -8.91%) better suits their portfolio needs.

    Sources indicate that bigBear.ai provides complex decision intelligence tools for federal and defense agencies, while Innodata helps major tech firms train generative AI systems. Both companies operate in the rapidly evolving world of artificial intelligence but serve different markets. This comparison examines their financial health, customer concentration, and valuation to help you decide which stock fits your strategy.

    BigBear.ai offers decision intelligence solutions that combine data from different sources to help leaders make faster choices. It serves critical sectors like national security, cybersecurity, and global supply chains. According to its latest annual report, a specific contract accounted for nearly 51% of consolidated revenue. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

    In a recent development, in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $142.1 million. This represented a revenue growth decline of approximately 1.5% compared to the prior period. The tech giant reported a net loss of roughly $180.2 million during this same time frame.

    According to recent reports, following its early 2026 debt conversion, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.0x, meaning the company carries virtually no debt relative to its equity. The current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term debts with short-term assets, is close to 1.8x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was negative at nearly $46.3 million.

    It has been revealed that innodata operates as a global data engineering firm that prepares and evaluates data for large-scale AI systems. The organization serves several high-profile technology leaders, with one customer in its digital data solutions segment accounting for nearly 58% of total revenue in 2025. This focus on the best small cap tech stocks in the data sector highlights its role in the generative AI boom.

    In a recent development, in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached approximately $350.2 million. This reflects a revenue growth increase of nearly 46.9% over the previous year. The organization also achieved a net income of roughly $48.5 million during this period.

    According to recent reports, as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio is approximately 2.7x. The debt-to-equity ratio is 0.0x, indicating a strong balance sheet with no total debt. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was nearly $35.6 million. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 23.8% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

    BigBear.ai faces significant risk due to heavy revenue concentration with government customers who can terminate contracts for convenience. Scaling its sales efforts remains a challenge while managing long and unpredictable sales cycles. It also faces intense competition from Microsoft (MSFT -2.77%) and Amazon (AMZN -4.10%). The manufacturer also navigates complex AI deployment risks and recent financial volatility including litigation over accounting errors.

    Innodata relies heavily on a single customer that contributed nearly 58% of its 2025 revenues, making it vulnerable to contract changes. It competes against well-resourced firms like Accenture (ACN +1.19%) and Cognizant Technology Solutions (CTSH +3.11%) in the data engineering space. The business also deals with geopolitical risks from its global workforce and ongoing legal challenges regarding securities class actions.

    Innodata appears to offer a more attractive value proposition based on its lower P/S ratio, which measures market value against sales over the past twelve months.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    It has been revealed that I'd go with Innodata. AI models are only as good as the data they learn from, and Innodata helps substantial tech companies create and test that data. Its sales have grown year over year for 13 straight quarters, and it makes money.

    Last quarter, sales jumped 53% and management raised its growth outlook, though the stock has fallen sharply this fall. There are risks: Two customers make up most of its sales, margins narrowed, and one program is winding down. But Innodata is adding newly introduced customers and work from a large cloud organization, and expects to replace the lost program by early next year.

    To give BigBear.ai its due, it does high-stakes work for national security and border security customers with contracts that are difficult to replace, and its backlog is growing. But it's still losing money, and government contract sales can be difficult to predict. That uncertainty is where Innodata stands apart: It is already profitable, with plenty of cash to keep investing as demand for AI data grows.

    Gadgets ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

    📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1029 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt.
    • High-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago.
    • The high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

    High-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

    The high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

    According to recent reports, spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

    According to recent reports, the high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

    Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," noted Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

    It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he noted.

    Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

    "The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone noted.

    He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

    That noted, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

    Industry observers note that "There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

    While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

    In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, mentioned Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

    According to recent reports, "We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she said.

    Industry observers note that the lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, mentioned Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

    The overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he stated. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

    In addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

    The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she noted.

    Industry observers note that "It is isolated," she noted. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

    For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

    "We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she said.

    Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

    In a recent development, but there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

    Recent findings suggest that "We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin stated. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

    It's also vital to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, noted R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

    "With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

    High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo mentioned.

    "That's when spreads really widen out," he remarked. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".

    By Will Healy – Nov 20, 2026 at 5:30PM EST.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Amazon (AMZN -4.10%), a global e-commerce, cloud, and digital advertising platform, closed at $246.82, down 4.10%. Shares fell on Friday amid an AI and mega-cap tech sell-off, while investors are watching capital spending, margins, and AWS growth.Trading volume reached 72.1M shares, coming in about 79% above its three-month average of 40.2M shares.     It has been revealed that S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) closed at 6,910, down 3.7%, while the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -5.28%) finished at 22,617, down 5.28%.     Negative sentiment from both its e-commerce and AWS segments seemed to weigh on Amazon stock today.

    Soft consumer spending and an increased need for promotional discounting led it to underperform retail counterparts like Walmart, which, as previously mentioned, rose in today's trading session.

    Recent findings suggest that moreover, capital expenditures (capex) continue to weigh on the stock. The manufacturer's proposal to spend $220 billion has led to free cash outflows, a concerning sign for a company that generated tens of billions in annual free cash flow until recently. Furthermore, despite a massive amount of liquidity, it has had to turn to the debt markets in a rising-rate environment.

    Such concerns were not unique to Amazon, and every stock in the Magnificent Seven, which contend with many of the same challenges, dropped today. Additionally, the Anthropic (ANT -8.50%) IPO has put AI in the spotlight this week. That stock has trended down since opening at $111.50 per share yesterday, likely adding to the negative sentiment surrounding AI.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Admittedly, at a P/E ratio of 20, Amazon stock looks like an increasingly attractive buy, arguably making it the one hyperscaler through 2030 that investors should buy and hold.     NBA one-month awards! MVP, best rookie, breakout stars and surprise teams so far

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2257 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • With the NBA season hitting the one-month mark, let's hand out some early awards!
    • Kelly Iko: Victor Wembanyama, with a sliiiight edge over Luka Dončić.
    • At this check-in, I have to go with Dončić after a month full of a variety pack of stepback 3s.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    With the NBA season hitting the one-month mark, let's hand out some early awards! Who has been the most valuable player so far? The best rookie? The league's breakout star? Our writers weigh in with their picks.

    Kelly Iko: Victor Wembanyama, with a sliiiight edge over Luka Dončić. Of players that have registered at least 300 minutes so far, the Spurs are 42.5 points per 100 possessions better with him on the floor, the most impactful in the league by some distance. (San Antonio looked like a fish out of water earlier this week when he was on the bench vs. Detroit.) He's also realized that, at 7-foot-4, his rim presence should be consistently weaponized. Per Second Spectrum, Wemby logged 65 alley-oop dunk attempts all of last season; he's at 40 before Thanksgiving. Add this growth to his continued defensive wizardry, along with taking care of the ball and improving as a creator, and you have yourself a solid argument.

    (Dillon Minshall/Yahoo Sports illustration).

    Steve Jones: Luka Dončić. At this check-in, I have to go with Dončić after a month full of a variety pack of stepback 3s. That's 38 points a night with defenses attempting to throw multiple schemes at him and it just hasn't mattered a ton yet. Combine that with him "doing his job" on defense, with more activity on switches and rotations; he's a significant reason why the Lakers are at the top of the West.

    Industry observers note that dan Devine: Luka Dončić. I'm with Steve, give me the league's leading scorer, the reason the Lakers have been consistently vying for the No. 1 offense in the NBA, and the driving force behind an L.A. team that couldn't get out of the first round last year being neck-and-neck with the conference champion Spurs and East-leading 76ers for the league's best record. For more information, consult your local library:.

    Nekias Duncan: Victor Wembanyama. I don't think you can go wrong with Dončić or Wembanyama, honestly, but 28-12-3-1-4 on 62 true shooting is absolutely nuts. Wemby's dunking everything in sight, making teams pay when they send help — his assist rate has risen, while his turnover rate has dropped from last year — and he's pretty easily been the most destructive defender in basketball this year. The "off" portion of Wemby's on-off numbers are insane, but I'd redirect to the "on" portion — the Spurs are outscoring teams by over 28 points per 100 possessions with him on the floor.

    Recent findings suggest that duncan: Cameron Boozer. With all due respect to Yaxel Lendeborg and Darius Acuff Jr. (don't let them boo you, massive dawg), I'll also be rolling with Mr. Boozer. I've been enamored with his processing speed and versatility all year long. He attacks or passes ahead of tilted defenses at a high level already. He's also showcased a willingness to let it fly from deep, a necessary buffer while he gets comfortable with his inside-the-arc work (he's converting 60% of his 2s over his last six games) against bigger players.

    Industry observers note that jones: Cameron Boozer. Rookie of the Year is going to continue to heat up as this season goes on, but Boozer's versatility offensively has delivered consistent impact for the Grizzlies. His ability to playmake fits right in with their identity: he can punish switches, and he can make plays on the short roll. There has rarely been a game where he hasn't left an imprint for a Grizzlies team that just keeps winning.

    Devine: Yaxel Lendeborg. I'm firmly on the record as very on-board for Boozer, who became the second-youngest player in NBA history to record a triple-double, but I'll give a shout out to Lendeborg. Yes, it's been a pretty brutal week for him, and for the Warriors as a whole, since Stephen Curry went down. But what he indicated in his first dozen games as a pro was truly eye-opening. Coming out of Michigan, the book on Yaxel was that, as a 24-year-old super-duper-senior, he'd have the experience, toolkit and physical maturity to be able to immediately fill a role in the league. I'm not sure anyone saw that role being "guy who can average an efficient 20-plus a night on high usage, and help elevate a team that just about everybody thought was drawing dead." That might not last forever, especially if Steph's absence stretches. But for the first month, it was an exceedingly pleasant surprise.

    Iko: Darius Acuff Jr. I'm not going to punish Acuff for being born into the Kings family. I'm also not going to magnify his low shot-making efficiency or assist-to-usage ratio in Sacramento. This kid is an absolute terror with the ball in his hands, averaging 26.2 points, 7.0 assists and 3.6 rebounds a night. In spite of Sacramento. You wanna know the list of folks to achieve benchmarks like that as a rookie? Wilt. Kareem. Jordan. Oscar Robertson. Elvin Hayes. Darius. His feel for the game, creation and scoring versatility is there — the rough edges will smoothen out as time goes on.

    Recent findings suggest that jones: Memphis Grizzlies. While the Sixers keep finding ways to win as they figure it out, and while the Lakers are at the top of the West, and the Wolves have stayed steady without Anthony Edwards, the Grizzlies being one game out of the top is something few saw coming. They are 8-0 on the road, which is not just the best road start in franchise history, but the longest road winning streak in franchise history. Let that sink in.

    Duncan: Houston Rockets, if for no other reason than to save you all from the massive victory lap I'd like to take over the Grizzlies. It's not a surprise that the Rockets are a good team; the way they've been good is simply not what I had on the bingo card. They have the league's best offense and a top-five half-court unit to boot — a notable shift from last year (7th overall, 19th in the half-court). This largely hasn't been the Kevin Durant show; this is the second lowest scoring (21.3) and lowest shot-taking (13.3 attempts) season of his career. The growth and empowerment of Alperen Şengün and Amen Thompson, the confidence and shot-making of Jabari Smith Jr. (career-best 38.8% from 3), and the return of the steady-handed Fred VanVleet has led to a more efficient, free-flowing offense.

    It has been revealed that iko: Houston Rockets. They have very quietly made a compelling case for being a top-5 team in the NBA. VanVleet's return has come with less control than he's accustomed to, but when you're converting shots at the highest efficiency of your career, who cares about usage rates? Smith is more confident in his in-between game and still has a knack for timely momentum-shifting splashes — as well as an unheralded five-position defensive skill set. They are second in offense and seventh in defense, don't turn the ball over, obliterate opponents on the offensive glass and still have a healthy Durant. Why couldn't they stick around until June?

    According to recent reports, devine: Portland Trail Blazers, in part because I'm an incorrigible shill who wants to deliver a ruthless plug for the big story he just wrote on Damian Lillard, and in part because I'm not sure anybody saw Portland sitting at 10-5 with a top-10 defense heading into opening night. Micah Nori's done a sensational job, Donovan Clingan and Toumani Camara look like bona fide linchpins, Jrue Holiday is always just what the doctor ordered, and Scoot Henderson even broke out against the Bucks on Thursday. Get Ja Morant back on the court, and Portland might just have a stew goin'.

    Devine: Toronto Raptors. It's not a shock to me that they are 5-10, given the myriad injuries they've suffered — most notably, obviously, getting just two games out of Kawhi Leonard before he went down with amorphous, ill-defined knee woes that, in a recent report by the great Michael Grange of Sportsnet, evoked the phrase "mystery condition." (Who could have foreseen this?!?) I do find it disappointing, though, that a team that won 46 games with the point differential of a 50-win squad and a top-seven defense last season — without Leonard — has so often looked so feckless this season … and that it's a combined 0-8 against teams with .500 or better records, getting blitzed by 11.5 points per 100 possessions against opponents with top-10 net ratings. Maybe, with better health, the Raptors will turn things around. Right now, though, even given the absence of their big-ticket offseason acquisition, they seem disappointingly unserious.

    Iko: Charlotte Hornets. There's no way you could have convinced me the Hornets would be 28th in net rating a week before Thanksgiving. I know the injuries to Kon Knueppel and Coby White have delayed what should have been a smooth start. But there's just something off about them when you watch, a level of disharmony and disjointedness that shouldn't be there this early in a season. Their collapse this week on the road in L.A., a game in which they led quite comfortably by 18 points deep into the second half, was embarrassing. The erasure of Brandon Miller, who has suddenly turned into a hybrid of Monta Ellis and J.R. Smith, is also jarring. Charles Lee has quite the tall task on his hands.

    Duncan: Utah Jazz, by default. Injuries have simply derailed this group. The playmaking and screening chops of Jusuf Nurkić were missing to begin the year, an underrated hit to what the Jazz want to establish. More pressing, they've had to navigate absences from Jaren Jackson Jr. and Lauri Markkanen. It's led to an offense that has felt rudderless at times — and easy to switch against — paired with a defense that isn't good enough to hold things together. I simply didn't think this would be a three-win team a month in.

    Recent findings suggest that jones: Cleveland Cavaliers. Per NBA.com, they are the No. 4 scoring team in the league (118.3), boasting the No. 5 offensive rating in the league (117.5), and it doesn't feel like it at all. For a team with this level of firepower, with the added bonus of continuity after an Eastern Conference finals run, the drink has felt flatter than usual. The Cavs likely just need a quick chat with momentum to turn things around, but I had high expectations for this group to take off or figure things out swiftly. It has felt stuck in the middle to me.

    Iko: Paul George. If this is intended for younger players, I apologize, but I'm in complete awe of what 36-year-old is doing right now in Boston. He's played next to Jayson Tatum for only a month, but their synergy screams of a lifelong partnership. He's still firing off eight 3s a night while converting them at the highest clip of his career; still serving as an effective secondary creator, scorer and connective tissue for MazzullaBall; and still one of the premier contest-without-fouling wings around. This was supposed to be a puzzling Celtics transaction, remember? Not acquiring a player nearing 40 who's still producing at a top-25 level. Color me shocked.

    Jones: Davion Mitchell. Just the term breakout star had me in a headlock; I wanted to go with KAT, but he's already broken out, Cooper Flagg has taken a leap, Franz Wagner is scoring and playmaking, and LaMelo Ball is playing defense. I'm going with Mitchell, leaning on the breakout portion of the program. He's been dynamic in transition and in pick-and-roll, finding his way into the paint consistently. The on-ball pressure remains tremendous and he's knocking down 3s. He's been exactly what the Heat have needed.

    In a recent development, duncan: Cedric Coward. (Davion Mitchell is such a tremendous shout!) Coward has simply been awesome for the Grizzlies to start the year. He's shooting the leather off the ball (45.2% on 5.2 attempts from 3), the drives have more juice, the passing has perked up, and he continues to add value as an offensive rebounder. On the other end, he's putting together a legitimate All-Defense campaign while consistently taking on tough assignments. As of this writing, opposing offenses are generating under 0.8 points per possession whenever Coward defends a ball screen (0.76), a handoff (0.76), or an off-ball screen (0.55). There's a reason the Grizzlies have been nearly 15 points better per 100 possessions with him on the floor.

    Devine: Holy crap, none of you guys said Ty Jerome? OK, then: Ty freaking Jerome!

    Recent findings suggest that there are five players in the NBA this season averaging at least 25 points and five assists per game on .600 true shooting, and Ty Jerome is the only one of them that 99% of NBA fans couldn't pick out of a lineup. (The other four: Luka, Giannis, Tyrese Maxey, Jamal Murray.) Sickos who do this for a living might have been aware that the eighth-year pro out of Virginia could be capable of this sort of production given health and opportunity, but it's certainly come as a shock to just about everybody else — including opponents of the Grizzlies who might've come into the season expecting things to be sweet only to find themselves on the business end of a steady diet of impossible floaters and 30-foot pull-up bombs. Memphis has been one of the best stories in the league this season, and its low-profile, high-octane point guard has been one of the biggest reasons why.

The digital transformation specialist's shares ended the day more than 4% higher.

    Sources indicate that globant's third-quarter revenue was $611.1 million, down 1% year over year. Non-IFRS (adjusted) net income also declined, falling by almost 9% to nearly $63.8 million, or $1.48 per share.

    That earnings per share (EPS) figure met analyst expectations while revenue notched a slight beat. The pundit top-line consensus for that line item was $610.9 million.

    According to recent reports, like the more progressive legacy software companies, Globant -- which specializes in developing custom software for enterprises automating aspects of their business -- has embraced artificial intelligence (AI) in its solutions. It said in its earnings release that its recently introduced AI Pods subscription service had doubled its annualized run rate.

    Globant quoted co-founder and CEO Martin Migoya as saying that "We are seeing growing enterprise adoption as clients shift from hourly billing toward outcome- and consumption-based delivery.".

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    In a recent development, it's one thing to embrace AI as either a tool for internal software development or to tack on some of its functionalities to an existing software suite. It's quite another to lead with it as a product offering, like Globant is doing with AI Pods.

    According to recent reports, the service is clearly resonating with the market, and I think it might soon become a driver of growth for this company given its relatively high margins. This is starting to look something like a sleeper stock among the many software titles on the market, and as such, it's well worth watching.

    Here's the Average Social Security Benefit at Age 67

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (661 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 20, 2026 at 6:00PM EST.
    • The average Social Security benefit for 67-year-olds is $2,016.48 per month, according to Social Security Administration (SSA) data from December 2025.
    • Sources indicate that reaching this age doesn't always mean you receive exactly 100% of your baseline amount.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 20, 2026 at 6:00PM EST.

    The average Social Security benefit for 67-year-olds is $2,016.48 per month, according to Social Security Administration (SSA) data from December 2025. Full retirement age (FRA) ranges from 66 to 67, depending on your birth year, and it's 67 for everyone born in 1960 or later. It's the point where you're eligible for your unreduced retirement amount.

    Sources indicate that reaching this age doesn't always mean you receive exactly 100% of your baseline amount. Many people who are 67 today have a full retirement age of 66 years and 10 months. These workers may have already earned small delayed retirement credits if they waited until 67 to claim their checks.

    According to recent reports, earnings histories also impact these averages. Men who are 67 receive an average of $2,234.41 per month, while the average among women is $1,801.82. This results in a monthly gender gap of $432.59 as of December 2025.

    Think of your full retirement age as the baseline for your benefits. The SSA bases your check on your average monthly income over your 35 highest-earning years, adjusting those wages for inflation and applying the primary insurance amount formula. This calculation creates the standard amount you're entitled to at full retirement age.

    It has been revealed that you don't have to claim at your baseline. You can earn delayed retirement credits, which are increases for delaying past FRA, worth 8% per year up to age 70. For a worker whose FRA is 67, waiting those three extra years provides a 24% total increase in monthly income.

    These decisions have a visible impact on the data. The average monthly benefit at age 70 is $2,274.68, which is $258.20 higher than the age-67 average.

    Industry observers note that but even for these claimants, benefits alone often aren't enough to live on. Social Security was only designed to replace about 40% of pre-retirement wages, so most retirees rely on savings or other income to cover their full costs.

    A 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) will take effect in 2027 to help benefits keep pace with inflation. This will add about $73 a month on top of the average listed above. These adjustments are designed to protect your purchasing power over time.

    Knowing the population average gives you a target for your own planning, but your final check depends on your career earnings and when you choose to claim.

    Sources indicate that waiting until age 67 to claim Social Security helps you avoid the early claiming benefit reduction, which can drastically reduce your checks. This is one major reason FRA is such a popular claiming age, but it's not the only one.

    When you claim Social Security under your FRA, you're also at risk of losing some of your benefits to the earnings test if you're still working. In 2027, for example, you lose $1 from your checks for every $2 you earn over $25,960 if you're under your FRA all year. If you'll reach your FRA next year, you only lose $1 for every $3 you earn over $67,920.

    It has been revealed that these lost benefits come back to you as a permanent benefit boost at your FRA. But for some, the risk of short-term losses makes them delay their claim until their FRA, when the earnings test no longer applies. This is something to weigh if you plan to continue working once you're eligible for Social Security checks.

    For more on how Social Security affects your retirement, see this guide.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 6:05PM EST.
    • Industry observers note that deciding between PayPal (PYPL -5.46%) and SoFi Technologies (SOFI -7.76%) requires balancing established market dominance against aggressive digital growth.
    • In a recent development, payPal remains a global giant in payment processing, while SoFi is a fast-growing digital bank targeting a younger, high-earning demographic.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 6:05PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than PayPal ›.

    Industry observers note that deciding between PayPal (PYPL -5.46%) and SoFi Technologies (SOFI -7.76%) requires balancing established market dominance against aggressive digital growth. Both companies are fighting for a larger share of your digital wallet today.

    In a recent development, payPal remains a global giant in payment processing, while SoFi is a fast-growing digital bank targeting a younger, high-earning demographic. While they operate in different niches, both compete for the same pool of consumer financial activity, making them frequent candidates for a fintech-focused portfolio as investors look toward the future of money.

    PayPal operates a massive digital payments platform serving nearly 439 million active accounts across 200 markets. It provides branded checkout services, person-to-person payments via Venmo, and even Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) trading within its app. This scale makes it one of the most recognizable names in fintech stocks today as it adapts to a changing financial landscape.

    Recent findings suggest that reliable recent quarterly figures for at least one of these companies aren't available, so this comparison uses each company's latest full fiscal year. For FY 2025, PayPal reported revenue of nearly $33.2 billion, representing growth of approximately 4.3% over the prior year. The company generated net income of close to $5.2 billion, showing a steady ability to convert its high volume of transactions into profit for its shareholders.

    Industry observers note that as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio reached roughly 0.5x, comparing total debt to shareholder equity. The current ratio, which compares short-term assets to short-term liabilities, was approximately 1.3x. Free cash flow, or the cash remaining after paying for operations and equipment, was nearly $5.6 billion in FY 2025.

    It has been revealed that soFi Technologies is a mobile-first financial services provider that offers a wide range of products including student loan refinancing, home loans, and investment tools. It serves approximately 15.8 million members and has expanded into business services through a partnership with Mastercard (MA -0.14%). The company also supports Bitcoin trading and provides modern banking infrastructure to other firms through its proprietary technology segments.

    For its latest annual report covering FY 2025, SoFi Technologies generated revenue of nearly $3.6 billion, which was an increase of approximately 35.1% compared to the previous year. The manufacturer reported net income of close to $481.3 million, marking a significant transition into consistent profitability. This growth was driven by a diversified mix of lending products and financial services that attracted new members to its platform.

    Sources indicate that based on its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was roughly 0.2x, helping investors see the low level of debt relative to shareholder equity. The current ratio was approximately 0.2x, which measures a company's ability to cover immediate liabilities with assets that can be quickly converted to cash. Free cash flow for the year was a net loss of nearly $4.0 billion, which often occurs in banking as capital is deployed into new loans rather than held as cash.

    Recent findings suggest that payPal faces intense competition from both traditional banks and newer technology platforms that offer digital checkout solutions. The manufacturer is also subject to extensive global regulatory oversight regarding payment processing and anti-money laundering rules. Any failure to manage cybersecurity risks or protect user data could lead to significant penalties and damage its reputation.

    SoFi Technologies must manage the complex regulatory requirements that come with being a bank holding firm. It relies on a concentrated number of whole loan purchasers, meaning its results could suffer if these buyers reduce their activity. Additionally, the company faces the challenge of managing rapid growth across its various lending and technology segments without increasing credit risks.

    When comparing these two companies using Forward P/E, PayPal looks significantly cheaper than its peer based on future earnings estimates.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    It has been revealed that I'd go with SoFi Technologies. Its sales and earnings are both growing far faster than PayPal's, and it has built a full digital bank with more than 17 million members, starting from student loans. Its bank charter lets it fund loans with its members' deposits, a cost advantage most fintech rivals lack.

    Industry observers note that soFi also gave investors its 2027 outlook a full quarter early, and it came in above analysts' expectations, with revenue expected to grow about 27%. Management built it assuming interest rates keep rising, even after a rate hike this year hurt the stock. The shares are still down for the year, so long-term investors get a lower price for a profitable, growing business.

    To give PayPal its due, it is a household name that produces plenty of cash, and Venmo is growing fast. But its original business, letting shoppers pay online with their PayPal account, is barely growing, and overall sales are rising slowly. By contrast, SoFi's lending and banking businesses are surging, and even its technology business, which lost a large client, is expected to return to growth in 2027. For long-term investors, that mix of growth, profits, and a lower price makes SoFi the better buy for 2027.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Plenty of companies are growing incredibly well right now, including several from the artificial intelligence business.
    • Except for orbital launch and satellite tech specialist Rocket Lab (RKLB -10.92%), it isn't.
    • Sources indicate that rocket Lab offers satellite launch solutions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By James Brumley – Nov 20, 2026 at 6:30PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Rocket Lab ›.

    Plenty of companies are growing incredibly well right now, including several from the artificial intelligence business. A tech giant that's set to triple its top line over the course of the next couple of years, though? That seems outrageous.

    Except for orbital launch and satellite tech specialist Rocket Lab (RKLB -10.92%), it isn't. This future business is already lined up. These paying customers are just waiting for one pivotal milestone that's likely to materialize sometime next year. Then the floodgates open.

    Sources indicate that rocket Lab offers satellite launch solutions. Its relatively small Electron rocket design has now been rolled out 100 times, putting 273 satellites into low earth orbit.

    The organization also provides a range of satellite components and construction services, which accounts for more than half of last quarter's revenue of $268 million. Rocket Lab expects to do around $980 billion in business in fiscal 2026, well up from last year's $602 billion.

    This is just a taste of what's to come, though. As the company announced with its third-quarter report posted earlier this month, Rocket Lab's backlog grew 52% from Q2's $2.36 billion to an incredible $3.6 billion. The organization just needs more capacity, but that's coming. Rocket Lab can now manufacture an Electron rocket every eight days.

    Recent findings suggest that then there's the proverbial 800-pound gorilla in the room. That's the company's larger Neutron rocket, which has seen its inaugural flight pushed back several times, with the first flight now expected sometime in 2027.

    Recent findings suggest that despite the delays so far, once Neutron is flying, everything takes a turn for the better. As CFO Adam Spice commented during the third-quarter's earnings conference call, adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) "will turn positive within six months of that first successful test flight," with cash flow likely to turn positive shortly after that.

    Industry observers note that neutron isn't the big profit center in and of itself, to be clear. It's just a means to an end. Being able to put larger, heavier satellites into orbit also opens up its satellite tech business. Of its new backlog of $3.6 billion, $1.7 billion of it reflects space systems rather than launch services, up 194% year over year.

    It has been revealed that to this end, while analysts aren't yet looking for Rocket Lab's revenue to triple between now and 2028, with recent failures of similar rockets like ULA's Vulcan and one earlier in the year from Blue Origin, Rocket Lab is swiftly becoming a preferred launch option. It may well exceed 2028's expectations.

    Recent findings suggest that as for the impact on the stock, it's not a complicated prediction to make. If the firm's top line comes anywhere close to tripling by 2028, the bullish argument firms up enormously.

    Recent findings suggest that while it may not triple in value in step with revenue, $3 billion in sales could turn this high-growth $34 billion outfit into a $60 billion outfit with relative ease. And given that the company isn't likely to raise money by issuing more stock anytime soon, that translates into a near-doubling of the stock's price.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Recent findings suggest that you're getting some help in the meantime, by the way. The analyst community overwhelmingly considers RKLB stock a strong buy right now, with a 12-month consensus price target of $93.30 already more than 80% above the ticker's current price.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • However, the vast universe of dividend stocks can make selection challenging.
    • Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Uncertainty in the Middle East, elevated Treasury yields and fears about an AI bubble continue to keep global markets on edge. Given this volatile backdrop, investors seeking stable income can consider enhancing their portfolios by adding dividend-paying stocks.

    However, the vast universe of dividend stocks can make selection challenging. Tracking the ratings of top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend stocks, as their recommendations are backed by in-depth research.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Chord Energy is an independent exploration and production firm with long-lived assets primarily in the Williston Basin. With a quarterly base dividend of $1.30 per share, CHRD offers a dividend yield of 3.67%.

    Sources indicate that in a research note on third-quarter expectations, RBC Capital analyst Scott Hanold reiterated a buy rating on CHRD stock with a price target of $175. "We model production near the top of guidance and continue to see strong performance from newly introduced wells and base production," said Hanold.

    According to recent reports, specifically, the five-star analyst expects Q3 2026 production at 283 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day, or Mboe/d, in line with the Street's consensus and near the high end of the 278 to 284 Mboe/d guidance. Hanold said his Q3 2026 earnings per share estimate increased to $5.29 due to lower non-cash depreciation, depletion and amortization.

    In a recent development, meanwhile, cash flow per share estimate moved lower to $13.59 to reflect Hanold's patch based on the current backdrop and commodity mark-to-market. He expects Chord Energy to report capital spending of $375 million for Q3 2026, slightly above the Street's estimate of $369 million.

    Sources indicate that overall, Hanold remains bullish on CHRD, given its best-in-class balance sheet. He expects a free cash flow payout of 80% in the third quarter, with the possibility of an upside. Hanold expects investors to focus on management commentary on 2027 capital aims, Williston M&A opportunities, and long-term performance of 4-mile wells.

    Hanold ranks No. 310 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 14.9%. See Chord Energy KPIs on TipRanks.

    Industry observers note that williams, an energy infrastructure manufacturer that delivers natural gas, is the next dividend pick. The company recently completed the $5.5 billion acquisition of Momentum Midstream, which will expand its natural gas infrastructure in the Haynesville to meet growing Gulf Coast LNG, power and industrial demand. At a quarterly dividend of $0.5250 per share, Williams offers a yield of 2.89%.

    According to recent reports, in her latest research note, RBC Capital analyst Elvira Scotto reiterated a buy rating on Williams stock with a price target of $87. Ahead of Q3 2026 earnings, the analyst remarked that she expects WMB to announce strong quarterly performance.

    Sources indicate that scotto raised her estimates to reflect insights from the quarterly catch-up call, the completion of the Momentum Midstream acquisition, and mark-to-market quarter-to-date commodity prices. She expects WMB to report Q3 2026 adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of $2,036 million, which is modestly above the Street's consensus estimate.

    Furthermore, Scotto expects Williams' Transmission, Power & Gulf segment to increase quarter-over-quarter, driven by the startup of the Socrates power project and favorable natural gas liquids, or NGL, margins.

    Industry observers note that scotto noted that WMB stock has underperformed due to backlash related to data centers and investor anticipation of another Power Innovation project. She expects the company to announce at least one more project before the end of this year, potentially with a new customer and a contract duration of 15 to 20 years, which would be a positive catalyst for the stock.

    Sources indicate that scotto ranks No. 175 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been profitable 67% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.2%. See Williams Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Recent findings suggest that EOG Resources, a crude oil and natural gas exploration and production organization, will hold its third-quarter earnings call on Nov. 6. At a quarterly dividend of $1.02 per share, EOG offers a dividend yield of 2.75%.

    Heading into Q3 earnings, Jefferies analyst Lloyd Byrne reiterated a buy rating on EOG Resources stock and increased his price target to $185 from $175. The analyst expects the company's Q3 cash flow per share to exceed the Street's consensus by 13%, driven by better-than-expected production.

    Byrne expects crude oil production, excluding the UAE, to reach 551 Mboe/d, which is at the high end of guidance (546-551 Mboe/d) and above the Street's projection of 548 Mboe/d, driven by continued growth in the Utica.

    Industry observers note that furthermore, Byrne expects cash operating expenses to come in at $10.27 per barrel of oil equivalent, below the midpoint of guidance of $10.05 to $11.35, helped by lower lease operating expenses. Overall, the analyst expects EOG to deliver free cash flow of $2.65 billion, supporting another quarter of buybacks near the minimum 70% shareholder return threshold and implying about $1.5 billion in share repurchases.

    "As a first indication of the '27 plan, we expect EOG will message another year of mid-single-digit (~3.5%) growth on a flat capital budget (~$6.55bn), which is above the Street modeling 1% oil growth at $6.6bn," said Byrne.

    Byrne ranks No. 303 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 58% of the time, delivering an average return of 18.5%. See EOG Resources Statistics on TipRanks.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Arizona Cardinals might be turning to their fourth quarterback of the season.
    • In a press conference, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur mentioned Carson Beck is dealing with back spasms and did not practice Friday.
    • "Not gonna shut the door on him [Beck], but we're gonna proceed as if Josh is gonna be starting on Sunday," LaFleur stated.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Arizona Cardinals might be turning to their fourth quarterback of the season.

    In a press conference, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur mentioned Carson Beck is dealing with back spasms and did not practice Friday. As a result, the team is preparing for backup Josh Johnson to be the team's starting quarterback for Week 11.

    "Not gonna shut the door on him [Beck], but we're gonna proceed as if Josh is gonna be starting on Sunday," LaFleur stated.

    Beck, who is a rookie, was thrust into the role of starter after Gardner Minshew went on injured reserve with a torn UCL. The Cardinals' original starter, Jacoby Brissett, was traded to the Baltimore Ravens after being benched for Minshew mid-game the week before.

    Beck was officially ruled as questionable in Friday's injury report.

    Industry observers note that laFleur remarked in his press conference that the team will monitor how Beck responds to treatment and how he feels on Saturday before making any final decisions. The coach added that this is an matter that Beck has dealt with before, but wasn't able to provide a clear timeline for Beck's return.

    In the meantime, Johnson, who was signed off the Cincinnati Bengals' practice squad after the Minshew injury, looks poised to be stepping up for Sunday's matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs.

    In a recent development, the itinerant backup quarterback also has some history with LaFleur: Johnson and LaFleur's careers overlapped in 2021, when both were with the Fresh York Jets (LaFleur was an offensive coordinator at the time). LaFleur had high praise for Johnson, noting some of the reasons he's been able to keep his career going this long.

    It has been revealed that "If it is Josh, I've called plays for him before, and had a really great experience calling plays for him," LaFleur stated. "He is incredible in the quarterback room, he's incredible for the starters. He's incredible for young quarterbacks, in terms of the way he sees the game, his energy, his positivity, how he keeps it real. He's mature. And he can still sling it. … If that's the route that ends up happening, let's go.".

    Industry observers note that arizona is the 15th NFL franchise that Johnson has been a part of in his career, as the 40-year-old quarterback has bounced between half of the teams in the league. Across 16 seasons, he has only started 11 games in his NFL career.

    Week 11 NFL betting buzz: Odds, sharp action and public betting splits

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Week 11 of the NFL season is already underway, which means it's time to research those bets for the weekend's matchups.

    We've compiled which teams the public is wagering on, along with some notable wagers, and asked several oddsmakers at various sportsbooks around the country to find out where the sharp action has come in for this weekend's games.

    Baltimore Ravens at Carolina Panthers (-3, 43.5).

    Upcoming Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears (-11.5, 48.5).

    Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs (-16, 41).

    Pittsburgh Steelers (-4, 37.5) at Philadelphia Eagles.

    Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-5.5, 45.5).

    Miami Dolphins at Buffalo Bills (-16.5, 44.5).

    Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys (-8, 55).

    Upcoming York Jets at Los Angeles Chargers (-3, 42).

    Check out all of Yahoo's sports betting content here in our upcoming betting hub.

    Jacksonville Jaguars (-6, 46.5) at Upcoming York Giants.

    Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10, 40).

    Minnesota Vikings at San Francisco 49ers (-3, 46.5).

    Cincinnati Bengals (-6, 54) at Washington Commanders.

    Here is where the betting public has landed on Week 10 games at BetMGM sportsbooks.

    Five most-bet sides (by total number of wagers).

    Five most-bet sides (by total dollars wagered).

    Most-bet totals (by total number of wagers).

    Minnesota Vikings at San Francisco 49ers Over 46.5.

    Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys Over 55.

    Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions Over 45.5.

    Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos Over 40.5.

    Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs Over 41.

    Most-bet underdogs to win (by total number of wagers).

    Most-bet anytime touchdown scorers (by total number of wagers).

    Joey Feazel, head NFL trader at Caesars Sportsbook: "Interesting one with the Baker Mayfield news. We reopened Lions -5.5 on Sunday afternoon, it's trickled out to -7. Bad news on the Aidan Hutchinson injury as well. Opened the total at 46.5, down to 44. Really just leaning on that Mayfield news and that Bucs have a solid defense. Right now, more Bucs action, but I anticipate the public being on the Lions, just depends what number they'll lay depending on Mayfield.".

    Thomas Gable, sportsbook director at The Borgata in Atlantic City: "This one has moved despite the injury to Hutchinson. This has moved from -5.5, up to -7. Obviously some uncertainty around Mayfield's health. Total has dropped from 46.5 to 44. Some decent early Lions money.".

    Feazel: "We've yet to see the Jaguars really stand out as a public team like the Lions or Bengals in attracting that public money. Jacksonville is our best case among AFC teams in the Super Bowl. A productive offense and can compete with the best of them. Two-way action thus far, a little bit more money on the Jaguars. I think we'll need the Giants, but not as much as some of the other top teams in our power ratings. Opened Jaguars -6, been bouncing back between -5.5 and -6. Opened 46.5 on the total and stayed at 46.5. Not the most action on this game.".

    Gable: "Jaguars opened -6.5, down to -6. We're probably going to get NY Giants money being situated here in Atlantic City as we have the past few weeks, and that's what it's been in the early going. Total opened 46.5, we're still sitting there. Probably going to end up needing the Jaguars to cover this number.".

    In a recent development, feazel: "This is looking like another Kyle McCord experience. Not a lot of action, people seeing Bills -16.5 and not wanting to go there. Little bit of money on the under and a little bit more spread money on the Dolphins. As the public gets involved, probably not going to get a ton of Miami love. Opened at Bills -16.5, it's still there even juiced a little on Buffalo. Opened total 47.5, now down to 45.5. Weather could be a factor.".

    It has been revealed that gable: "Biggest spread on the board right now. We opened at Bills -17, down to -16.5. Total has dropped two points, from 47 down to 45. Buffalo is in a ton of money-line parlays as you'd expect — the Bills and the Chiefs are two legs of many parlays. It's actually pretty balanced action on the spread.".

    It has been revealed that vikings vs. 49ers (in Mexico City).

    Feazel: "Really prolific 49ers offense versus very stingy Vikings defense. Even against the Packers last week, we haven't seen public gravitate towards Minnesota. We saw 49ers put up 46 points against Cowboys, but allowed 40. Likely going to need the Vikings here. It'll be all over money and a lot of 49ers money, as we approach Sunday night.".

    Gable: "We opened 49ers -3.5, quickly went to -3. Total sitting around 46 or 46.5, not much movement there. This game is interesting for a number of different reasons. It's in Mexico City at altitude. For a 49ers game, you have travel differences between the two teams again. And then you have the piece where Kirk Cousins just faced this defense a few weeks ago with the Raiders. The public has been on the 49ers here, but it's still very early.".

    According to recent reports, feazel: "Second-biggest total on the board at 54.5. As you'd expect, Bengals money and the over. Don't blame anyone for that, it's been easy money to back that. Defense was stingy against the Steelers. We've seen some movement towards Cincinnati. We opened Bengals -4.5, it's up to -6.5. Total opened at 52.5, up to 54.5. A flood of money on Bengals money and over. Don't anticipate that changing in this one.".

    Recent findings suggest that gable: "No surprise, this has been straight Cincinnati money since we opened it. Opened Bengals -4, that was before the Sunday night game against Pittsburgh. We adjusted the rating, moved the number up. Anything less than -6.5, people have been laying on the Bengals. It's even public money at -6.5 on Cincinnati. Total has jumped from 51.5 at the open to 54 presently.".

    Industry observers note that it's always notable where respected bettors have landed on this week's games. While these prices may not at the moment be available at all sportsbooks, knowing where sharps have wagered can also be instructive for in-game wagering.

    Yahoo Sports conversed with several bookmakers across the country, and here is where some sharp action has been (and the numbers it came in at):.

    Titans +8, Cowboys-Titans over 54.5.

    NY Jets +3.5, Chargers-NY Jets over 40.5, under 42.5.

    We'll be keeping track of six-figure (and larger) Week 11 NFL bets from sportsbooks, as well as if they end up cashing.
